chapters.title: Kosten im Griff
chapters.topic: FinOps and cloud cost management: budgets, tagging, rightsizing, savings plans and cost transparency for finance teams

terms.d: Adjusting cloud resources to match actual usage so you don't pay for idle capacity.
terms.ex: A quick rightsizing exercise cut their compute bill by a fifth.

terms.d: Labelling cloud resources with metadata such as cost centre or owner.
terms.ex: Without consistent tagging, nobody knows which department is driving the costs.

terms.d: Billing internal departments for the cloud resources they actually use.
terms.ex: Finance wants a chargeback model by the next budget cycle.

terms.d: Showing departments their cloud costs without actually charging them.
terms.ex: We usually start with showback before moving to chargeback.

terms.d: A commitment to a fixed hourly spend in exchange for lower prices.
terms.ex: A savings plan makes sense once the workloads are stable.

terms.d: An unexpected spike in spending that needs investigation.
terms.ex: The alert flagged a cost anomaly in the test subscription over the weekend.

terms.d: An automatic notification when spending approaches a set limit.
terms.ex: Let's set a budget alert at eighty percent for every project.

terms.d: Costs and revenue measured per unit, such as per customer or per transaction.
terms.ex: The CFO cares less about the total bill and more about unit economics.

terms.d: Charges for data transferred out of a cloud region or network.
terms.ex: Remember to factor egress costs into the architecture.

terms.d: Cloud resources that are running but not doing useful work.
terms.ex: We found dozens of idle resources left over from old pilots.

phrases: Let's look at where the money is actually going before we cut anything.
Kostenanalyse vorschlagen
The quickest win is usually switching off what nobody uses.
Quick Win benennen
Can we agree on a tagging policy before the next migration wave?
Governance anstoßen
Predictable costs matter more to you than the lowest price, is that fair to say?
Bedarf bestätigen
I'll send you a breakdown by subscription so finance can see the trend.
Follow-up zusagen
We can cap the risk with budgets and alerts from day one.
Kostenangst nehmen

chapters.title: Sicherheit & Zero Trust
chapters.topic: cloud security conversations: zero trust, identity and access, threats like phishing and ransomware, and incident response

terms.d: A security model that verifies every access request instead of trusting the network.
terms.ex: Zero trust means we check every login, even from inside the office.

terms.d: Signing in with a second proof of identity in addition to a password.
terms.ex: Enforcing multi-factor authentication would have stopped this attack.

terms.d: Giving users only the access they need for their job.
terms.ex: Admins should work with least privilege and request higher rights only when needed.

terms.d: Rules that allow or block access based on user, device, location or risk.
terms.ex: With conditional access, unmanaged devices can only open email in the browser.

terms.d: All the points where an attacker could try to get into a system.
terms.ex: Every public endpoint increases the attack surface.

terms.d: The overall strength of an organisation's security setup.
terms.ex: The assessment gives you a score for your current security posture.

terms.d: The process of detecting, containing and recovering from a security breach.
terms.ex: Do you have an incident response plan that has actually been tested?

terms.d: Fake messages designed to trick people into revealing data or clicking malicious links.
terms.ex: Most breaches still start with a simple phishing email.

terms.d: Malware that encrypts data and demands payment to unlock it.
terms.ex: Immutable backups are your best insurance against ransomware.

terms.d: Protecting stored data by encrypting it on disk.
terms.ex: All customer data is protected by encryption at rest by default.

phrases: Who can access this data today, and how would you know if that changed?
Bedarf aufdecken
Security is usually the reason to move, not the reason to wait.
Einwand umdrehen
Let's start with identity, because that's where most attacks begin.
Priorität setzen
Would it help if our security architect joined the next call?
Experten einbinden
We can map this against the controls your auditors already use.
Compliance verbinden

chapters.title: Daten & Analytics
chapters.topic: data platforms and analytics: breaking down data silos, data quality, pipelines, dashboards and data governance

terms.d: A central environment for storing, processing and analysing an organisation's data.
terms.ex: A modern data platform is the foundation for any serious AI project.

terms.d: Data kept in separate systems that don't talk to each other.
terms.ex: Sales and service still work in data silos, so nobody sees the full customer.

terms.d: One agreed place where the correct version of data lives.
terms.ex: The board wants a single source of truth for revenue figures.

terms.d: How accurate, complete and up to date data is.
terms.ex: Poor data quality will undermine the best dashboard.

terms.d: An automated flow that moves and transforms data between systems.
terms.ex: The data pipeline refreshes the sales figures every hour.

terms.d: Analysing data as it arrives instead of in batches.
terms.ex: Real-time analytics lets the plant react before a machine fails.

terms.d: A visual overview of key figures on one screen.
terms.ex: The regional managers check the dashboard every Monday morning.

terms.d: Rules and responsibilities for how data is managed and used.
terms.ex: Data governance decides who may see salary information.

terms.d: Business users building their own reports without help from IT.
terms.ex: Self-service BI took a lot of pressure off the IT team.

terms.d: An inventory that describes what data exists and where it lives.
terms.ex: Start with a data catalogue so people can find what already exists.

phrases: What decisions would you make differently if you had this data every morning?
Nutzen herausarbeiten
Let's start with one report everyone already argues about.
Pragmatischer Einstieg
AI is only as good as the data behind it.
Daten als Basis betonen
Who owns this data today, IT or the business?
Verantwortung klären
Could you share a sample so our architect can take a look?
Nächsten Schritt einleiten

chapters.title: Regulierung & Compliance
chapters.desc: DSGVO, DORA, NIS2, EU AI Act
chapters.topic: regulation and compliance conversations with Austrian customers: GDPR, DORA, NIS2, the EU AI Act, audits and third-party risk

terms.d: Meeting the laws, regulations and standards that apply to a business.
terms.ex: Compliance is the first question in every banking workshop.

terms.d: A record that shows who did what and when.
terms.ex: The regulator expects a complete audit trail for every change.

terms.d: A contract that defines how a provider processes personal data on a customer's behalf.
terms.ex: Legal has asked for our data processing agreement before the pilot starts.

terms.d: A structured evaluation of what could go wrong and how likely it is.
terms.ex: We'll support your risk assessment with our documentation.

terms.d: A plan for how to move away from a provider if needed.
terms.ex: DORA requires banks to have a realistic exit strategy for critical providers.

terms.d: Risks that come from relying on external suppliers.
terms.ex: Third-party risk is now a standing item on the board agenda.

terms.d: Official confirmation that a service meets a specific standard.
terms.ex: You'll find every certification in our trust centre.

terms.d: Under the EU AI Act, an AI system used in sensitive areas that has stricter obligations.
terms.ex: A credit-scoring model would likely count as a high-risk AI system.

terms.d: Any information that can identify a person.
terms.ex: The chatbot must not store personal data longer than necessary.

terms.d: The authority that supervises an industry.
terms.ex: The regulator will want to see how you monitor the provider.

phrases: Which regulations are top of mind for your team this year?
Prioritäten erfragen
We can provide the documentation your auditors usually ask for.
Unterstützung anbieten
Let's involve your compliance team early rather than at the end.
Stakeholder einbinden
This doesn't remove your responsibility, but it makes it much easier to prove.
Ehrliche Einordnung
I'd suggest we map your requirements to our controls in a short workshop.
Workshop vorschlagen

chapters.title: Copilot-Einführung
chapters.topic: rolling out Copilot and AI assistants: adoption, change management, pilot groups, champions, the works council and measuring success

terms.d: How widely and actively people use a new tool.
terms.ex: Licences are easy to buy; adoption is the hard part.

terms.d: Preparing and supporting people through a change in how they work.
terms.ex: Without change management, the rollout will feel like just another IT project.

terms.d: A small group that tests a solution before a wider rollout.
terms.ex: We picked a pilot group from finance, sales and HR.

terms.d: Enthusiastic employees who help colleagues adopt a new tool.
terms.ex: The champions network answered most questions before they reached IT.

terms.d: Time or effort saved thanks to a new way of working.
terms.ex: We measured productivity gains in meeting preparation and email.

terms.d: The instruction or question you give an AI assistant.
terms.ex: A good prompt includes the context, the goal and the format you want.

terms.d: The step-by-step introduction of a solution across an organisation.
terms.ex: The rollout will happen in three waves over six months.

terms.d: Employee representatives who must be consulted on certain workplace changes.
terms.ex: In Austria, the works council should be involved early in any AI project.

terms.d: Agreed measures that show whether a project worked.
terms.ex: Let's define the success metrics before the pilot starts.

terms.d: Content that is accessible to more people than intended.
terms.ex: Fix oversharing in SharePoint before switching on Copilot for everyone.

phrases: Which three tasks eat up most of your team's week?
Use Cases finden
Let's agree on how we'll measure success before anyone gets a licence.
Erfolg messbar machen
The technology is ready; the question is whether your people are.
Change-Thema ansprechen
I'd involve the works council from the start to build trust.
Betriebsrat einbinden
We've seen the best results when managers use it first.
Best Practice teilen

chapters.title: Partner & Co-Sell
chapters.desc: Marketplace, Joint Business Plan, Deal Registration
chapters.topic: working with partners: systems integrators, managed service providers, the marketplace, joint business plans and deal registration

terms.d: The network of companies that build, sell and deliver solutions with a vendor.
terms.ex: Our partner ecosystem in Austria covers almost every industry.

terms.d: A partner that designs and implements complex IT solutions.
terms.ex: The systems integrator will handle the migration itself.

terms.d: A partner that runs and maintains IT services for a customer.
terms.ex: Many mid-sized customers prefer a managed service provider to run their environment.

terms.d: An online store where customers buy partner solutions through their cloud agreement.
terms.ex: Buying through the marketplace can count towards their existing commitment.

terms.d: A customer-specific price or term offered by a partner on the marketplace.
terms.ex: The partner created a private offer with a three-year discount.

terms.d: A shared plan with targets, accounts and activities agreed with a partner.
terms.ex: Let's review the joint business plan at the end of each quarter.

terms.d: Officially recording a partner's opportunity to protect it and unlock benefits.
terms.ex: Please complete the deal registration before the customer workshop.

terms.d: The plan for how a solution will be sold and to whom.
terms.ex: Our go-to-market for this offer focuses on manufacturing in Upper Austria.

terms.d: Passing a sales opportunity from one company to another.
terms.ex: We received a referral from the partner for a hospital group in Graz.

terms.d: Money a vendor provides to support workshops or pilots.
terms.ex: There's funding available for an envisioning workshop.

phrases: Who owns the customer relationship in this account?
Rollen klären
Let's pick three target accounts we both believe in.
Fokus setzen
What do you need from us to move faster?
Unterstützung anbieten
I'd like to align on next steps before either of us contacts the CIO.
Abstimmung sichern
Can you register the deal so we can unlock the funding?
Prozess anstoßen

chapters.title: Mit dem C-Level sprechen
chapters.topic: executive communication with CEOs, CFOs and CIOs: short key messages, business outcomes, trade-offs and decisions

terms.d: A short overview of the key points for senior decision-makers.
terms.ex: Put the executive summary on the first slide, not the last.

terms.d: The most important point or result.
terms.ex: The bottom line is that the project pays for itself in two years.

terms.d: The main point you want people to remember.
terms.ex: The key takeaway for the board is lower risk, not new technology.

terms.d: A goal that leadership has decided is most important.
terms.ex: Is cost reduction still your strategic priority for next year?

terms.d: Giving up one thing to gain another.
terms.ex: The trade-off is a slightly longer timeline for much lower risk.

terms.d: A plan that shows the main steps and milestones over time.
terms.ex: We'll share a twelve-month roadmap after the workshop.

terms.d: The benefit gained compared with the money spent.
terms.ex: The CFO asked for the return on investment in one sentence.

terms.d: A senior person who supports a project and removes obstacles.
terms.ex: Without an executive sponsor, the project will stall at the first budget question.

terms.d: How quickly a customer sees results after starting.
terms.ex: Time to value matters more to them than feature lists.

terms.d: A very short, persuasive summary you could give during a lift ride.
terms.ex: Practise an elevator pitch for when you meet the CEO at the event.

phrases: I'll keep this short: three points, then your questions.
Klarer Einstieg
What would make this a success for you personally?
Persönliches Ziel erfragen
In one sentence: lower risk, faster delivery, predictable costs.
Kernbotschaft
The decision we need from you today is whether to start the pilot.
Entscheidung einfordern
Happy to go deeper on any of this with your team.
Details delegieren

chapters.title: Einkauf & Ausschreibung
chapters.topic: procurement and tenders: requests for proposal, public tenders, contract terms, approvals and legal review

terms.d: The department or process responsible for buying goods and services.
terms.ex: Procurement will want three competing offers.

terms.d: A formal document asking vendors to submit offers.
terms.ex: The request for proposal is due on the fifteenth.

terms.d: A formal invitation to bid, especially in the public sector.
terms.ex: The tender includes strict requirements on data location.

terms.d: The rules that apply to a contract.
terms.ex: Their lawyers are still reviewing the terms and conditions.

terms.d: When and how payment must be made.
terms.ex: They asked for ninety-day payment terms.

terms.d: Formal approval from the person responsible.
terms.ex: We're waiting for the final sign-off from the CFO.

terms.d: A long-term contract that sets the terms for future orders.
terms.ex: They can order through the existing framework agreement.

terms.d: A small group of vendors still in the selection process.
terms.ex: Good news: we made the shortlist.

terms.d: Changes a party proposes to a contract draft.
terms.ex: Legal sent back the contract with redlines on liability.

terms.d: The factors used to compare and score offers.
terms.ex: Price is only thirty percent of the evaluation criteria.

phrases: Could you share the evaluation criteria so we can focus on what matters to you?
Kriterien erfragen
Who else needs to sign off before the order can go out?
Freigabeprozess klären
We can work within your framework agreement to keep this simple.
Hürden senken
I understand procurement needs alternatives; let's make the comparison fair.
Wettbewerb ansprechen
Let's agree on a realistic timeline for legal review.
Zeitplan absichern

chapters.title: Workshops & Präsentationen
chapters.topic: running customer workshops and presentations: agendas, facilitation, breakout sessions, handling questions and wrapping up

terms.d: The list of topics to cover in a meeting.
terms.ex: Let me quickly run through the agenda.

terms.d: A workshop to explore possibilities and define a vision with the customer.
terms.ex: The envisioning workshop produced fifteen use cases.

terms.d: The person who guides a workshop or discussion.
terms.ex: As facilitator, I'll keep an eye on the time.

terms.d: A short session in smaller groups within a larger meeting.
terms.ex: We'll start a breakout session for each department after the coffee break.

terms.d: A board, physical or digital, for drawing and writing ideas.
terms.ex: Let's sketch the current architecture on the whiteboard.

terms.d: Involving active practice rather than just theory.
terms.ex: The afternoon is hands-on, so please bring your laptops.

terms.d: A short summary of what has been discussed.
terms.ex: Here's a quick recap before we move on.

terms.d: A list of topics to discuss later so the meeting stays on track.
terms.ex: Good point, let's put it in the parking lot for now.

terms.d: To finish a meeting or discussion.
terms.ex: Let's wrap up with the next steps.

terms.d: A session where the audience asks questions.
terms.ex: We'll leave fifteen minutes for Q&A at the end.

phrases: Before we start, what would make today worthwhile for you?
Erwartungen klären
Let me pause here: does this match what you're seeing?
Interaktion herstellen
That's a great question; let's park it and come back after lunch.
Fokus halten
To sum up, we agreed on three use cases and a pilot date.
Ergebnisse sichern
I'll send the slides and a short summary by tomorrow.
Follow-up ankündigen

chapters.title: Projekte & Delivery
chapters.topic: project delivery language: milestones, go-live, dependencies, scope creep, steering committees and status updates

terms.d: An important point or event in a project timeline.
terms.ex: The first milestone is the landing zone sign-off.

terms.d: The moment a system starts being used for real work.
terms.ex: Go-live is planned for the first weekend in March.

terms.d: Something that must happen before another task can start.
terms.ex: The network upgrade is a dependency for the migration.

terms.d: Gradual, uncontrolled growth of a project's scope.
terms.ex: We need to watch for scope creep in the reporting requirements.

terms.d: A senior group that guides a project and makes key decisions.
terms.ex: The steering committee meets every four weeks.

terms.d: Passing responsibility for something to another person or team.
terms.ex: The handover to operations happens two weeks after go-live.

terms.d: A short report on progress, risks and next steps.
terms.ex: Could you send a status update before the steering committee?

terms.d: A list of project risks with owners and actions.
terms.ex: Let's add the licence delay to the risk register.

terms.d: A concrete output a project must produce.
terms.ex: The main deliverable of phase one is a tested architecture.

terms.d: Progressing as planned.
terms.ex: Overall we're on track, with one open risk.

phrases: We're on track overall, but there's one risk I want to flag.
Status mit Risiko
What's the impact if this slips by two weeks?
Auswirkung klären
That sounds like a change in scope; shall we assess it properly?
Scope Creep ansprechen
Who needs to approve this before we continue?
Entscheidung einholen
Let's agree on owners and dates for each action.
Verbindlichkeit schaffen

chapters.title: Modernisierung & Apps
chapters.topic: application modernisation: legacy systems, technical debt, containers, Kubernetes, microservices, serverless and DevOps

terms.d: Updating existing applications to use modern cloud technologies.
terms.ex: Application modernisation is where the long-term savings are.

terms.d: An old system that is still in use but hard to maintain.
terms.ex: The legacy system runs on hardware that's out of support.

terms.d: Future work caused by quick fixes or outdated technology.
terms.ex: Every year they wait, the technical debt grows.

terms.d: A lightweight package that bundles an application with everything it needs to run.
terms.ex: Packaging the app in a container makes it easy to move.

terms.d: An open-source platform for running and managing containers at scale.
terms.ex: Their developers already know Kubernetes, which helps a lot.

terms.d: An architecture where an application is split into small independent services.
terms.ex: Moving to microservices only makes sense if the teams are ready.

terms.d: Running code without managing servers; you pay only when it runs.
terms.ex: For irregular workloads, serverless can be very cost-effective.

terms.d: A way of working that brings development and operations together to deliver faster.
terms.ex: DevOps practices cut their release cycle from months to weeks.

terms.d: Automated building, testing and deployment of software.
terms.ex: With a CI/CD pipeline, every change is tested automatically.

terms.d: To restructure code without changing what it does.
terms.ex: We'd refactor the billing module first.

phrases: Which applications cause the most pain when you need to change them?
Schmerzpunkte finden
We don't need to modernise everything; let's start where change is most frequent.
Priorisieren
What skills does your team already have in-house?
Fähigkeiten klären
Lift and shift now, modernise later, is a perfectly valid plan.
Pragmatik
Let's look at the cost of doing nothing as well.
Kosten des Stillstands

terms.d: Meeting people to build professional relationships.

terms.d: Light, friendly conversation about everyday topics.
terms.ex: A bit of small talk about the ski season always works in Austria.

terms.d: A question or activity that helps people start talking.
terms.ex: Asking about their keynote is an easy icebreaker.

terms.d: The main speech at a conference or event.

terms.d: A small card with your contact details.

terms.d: To talk to someone you haven't spoken to for a while.

terms.d: To present one person to another.

terms.d: An action taken after a first contact to continue the conversation.

terms.d: A person you both know.

Gesprächseinstieg

Höflich abschließen
